## Text above a picture

The text before a picture stacks above it, as in HTML and the PDF.

- A bullet over the picture

![A picture under its text](images/example.jpg){width="40%"}

## A paragraph above a table

One paragraph across the content area, above the table, long enough to reach the right edge of the slide's body.

| Queue    | Nodes | Wall time |
|----------|------:|----------:|
| main     | 2,488 |     12 h  |
| develop  |   168 |      6 h  |
| preempt  | 2,488 |     24 h  |

## A footnote after a table in a column

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
The table's column keeps the line after its table.
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
| Queue   | Nodes | Share  |
|---------|------:|-------:|
| main    | 2,488 | 87.1 % |
| develop |   168 |  5.9 % |

† Nodes as of the last maintenance.
:::
::::

## A paragraph before columns

One line across the slide, then two columns.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column}
- The left column
:::
::: {.column}
- The right column
:::
::::

## A linked picture and a list

[![](images/example.jpg){width="35%"}](https://www.nasa.gov)

- A list after the linked picture
- Stays on its slide

## A note under a wrapped table

| Setting  | What it does |
|----------|--------------|
| select   | Chunks of nodes, each with its cores, memory and GPUs |
| walltime | The longest the job may run, after which the scheduler stops it and frees its nodes for the next job in the queue |

::: note
The last row wraps; the note sits under it.
:::

## Narrow columns of a table

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
| Group | Share | Of the allocation |
|-|-|----|
| COMMUNITY | 41.2 % | Allocated through the community panel, reviewed twice a year |
| UNIVERSITY | 30.5 % | Allocated to university researchers through their proposals |
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
Its lines pass 72 characters, so the dash runs set its widths: narrow first columns, and no word breaks inside a cell.
:::
::::

## A full figure {.full}

A caption wider than the body's margins allow, inside its own box: the slide less a narrow pad, as HTML lays it out.

## A lead above a picture

::: {.lead}
**A lead over the picture.** It stacks above it, as text does.
:::

![A picture under a lead](images/example.jpg){width="40%"}

> A quote under the picture stays on the slide.
